Cafe Goencho, Pali Hill is an absolute Goan food heaven! 🌴🔥 From the moment you walk in, the cozy, old-school Goan vibe wraps you in warmth and nostalgia — it feels like stepping straight into a Goan home kitchen.

The Poieto here is the real show-stopper — rich, soulful, and packed with deep, authentic flavors. Slow-cooked to perfection, it’s comforting, hearty, and incredibly satisfying. featured_reviews.name: Gokulraj
featured_reviews.review_text:
⭐ Jimi’s Burger, Bandra
Visited Jimi’s Burger, Bandra with a group of 4. Each of us ordered one burger, plus one combo with a drink and one starter. Overall, the experience was really good and worth the visit.

🍔 Burgers:

#Chicken Supreme Burger – 4.5/5
The taste was amazing! Very flavourful, loaded with cheese, and the fried chicken was perfectly cooked. Definitely a must-try.

#Daebak Fried Chicken Burger – 3.5/5
Good, spicy, and Korean-style, but slightly too oily for my taste. The Korean sauces were a bit overpowering, which dulled the overall flavour. Still decent if you like bold, saucy burgers.

#Chicken Smash Hit Burger – 5/5
Absolutely loved this one! Small, juicy, and super tasty. This was my first chicken smash burger, and it was cooked perfectly with great flavour.

#Veg Jaw Breaker (Double Patty) – 4.5/5
The name says it all! Huge burger and definitely difficult to eat in one bite 😄
It’s the costliest veg option but worth it stuffed with paneer, patties, and veggies. Very filling and tasty.

🧀 Starters:

Mozzarella Cheese Sticks – 4.5/5
Crispy on the outside, gooey on the inside. Pure cheese taste and fried really well.

🍟 Sides & Drinks:

Peri Peri Fries & Mojito – 4.5/5
Both were really good and complemented the burgers nicely.

⏰ Crowd & Location:

We went on a Saturday evening, so it was quite crowded. Had to wait around 20 minutes for seating.

Reaching Bandra itself can take time on weekends. Parking info isn’t clear we came by auto.

📍 Other Outlets:
They also have outlets in Thane, Vashi, Malad, and Andheri.

Overall: Great food, especially the chicken burgers. Slight wait time on weekends, but totally worth it for burger lovers 🍔🔥

featured_reviews.name: Adriel Fernandes
featured_reviews.review_text:
A burger joint that actually lives up to the hype!

Good Flippin' Burgers is easily one of my top picks when it comes to a no-nonsense, satisfying burger experience. The patties are juicy, flavourful, and clearly made with care — no dry, overcooked nonsense here. The buns are soft yet hold everything together perfectly (no collapsing halfway through your meal!), and the balance of sauces, cheese, and toppings hits the sweet spot.

The fries are golden, crisp, and addictive, especially the Peri Peri ones; and if you’re into sides, their chicken tenders and absolutely superb. For me, it's the sides that actually steal the show.

What I also love is the consistency. Whether you're dining in or ordering in, the quality doesn't drop. Service is usually quick, and the vibe is casual, clean, and efficient, exactly what you want from a great burger spot.

Highly recommend the “The Clucknator” or the “The Koren Krossover Ckikin burger 456”.

Tried both their Flippinade flavours, Cranberry and Lemon. The cranberry was surprisingly refreshing and gets a solid 4/5 from me. The lemon was okay, not bad, but didn’t quite hit the same mark 3/5.

These folks don’t just flip burgers, they nail the.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Frisbee in Bandra, and here’s the honest take… it’s small, crowded, slightly chaotic… but the food makes it worth it.
We began with their super spicy chicken strips, and when I say spicy, I mean fire-level heat. Crispy on the outside, juicy inside, and unapologetically bold, definitely not for the faint-hearted.
Next came the mini sliders, which I absolutely loved. The chicken was tender, flavorful, and perfectly balanced within those soft buns. Bite-sized, but packed with taste.
The real highlight, though, was the Nashville chicken burger. I’ve tried Nashville style chicken at many places, but this one was on a completely different level. The spice, the crunch, the juiciness, everything just worked. Easily one of the best I’ve had. And their fries deserve credit too, golden, crisp, and addictive.
The drinks were fairly average, your standard mojitos and regular options. Nothing bad, just nothing extraordinary.

The only downside? Space. It’s a very small outlet, and you often end up waiting outside for an hour or more. Inside, it can feel quite congested. But once you get your food, the wait starts making sense.

I hae been a regular at EAC since 2019. It has been my go-to for years, and while it remains a staple in my Bandra circuit, have noticed some shifts lately that are hard to ignore.
The freshness of their ingredients is honestly amazing - you can taste the quality in every bite. Over the years, I have tried almost everything on the menu across all sections, except for their new bread menu and the salads.
​The Food Journey
​When it comes to the food, I have had nearly all their desserts. If they have the Opera Pastry, it is a absolute must-try. On the other hand, the Tiramisu was just average. If you're going for a drink, the Pineapple Coriander Cooler and the Spiced Mojito are my absolute favorites, but the Vietnamese Cold Coffee is extremely bad - a hard skip.
For mains, their Chicken Burgers, especially the Peri Peri and Grilled Chicken, are top-notch. The Paneer Roasted Veggie Sandwich is also amazing. If you are there for breakfast, the Eggs Benedict is definitely the highlight.
​Pro Tip: You have to try their Roast Chicken with Mashed Potatoes; it is easily their most famous and iconic dish. Hard skip - anything fish.
However, lately, I have noticed the quality seems to have taken a dip. It is not a massive drop, but they have been increasing their SKUs (adding more items), and it is hard not to notice that the consistency isn't what it used to be.
The seating layout here is easily the best of any cafe in Bandra, but a recent experience with the crowd has made me think about stopping my visits completely.
​We were sitting near a table that was loud - uncomfortably loud. A man accompanied by two ladies spent hours shouting. It started with "India vs. Pakistan" and how "we will decimate them," then moved to "India vs. USA" and how the USA is so much better. It turned ugly when he started shitting on Hinduism, calling it a "pagan religion" and preaching Christianity. He kept saying India is "poor, filthy, and bad" because of Hindus and that people should go to churches to "get civilized."
It was highly uncomfortable and left us feeling genuinely shook. I took three weeks to think about whether I should even post this, but the experience was that bad.

Time to hunt for a new go to place.

Recently I visited Miya Kebab and I absolutely loved the food there. The place has some really unique and flavorful dishes.

On the positive side, the Tiger Fries were absolutely fabulous—perfectly done and very enjoyable. The Takoyaki chicken was okayish, but there’s room for improvement.

featured_reviews.name: Smridhi Sharma
featured_reviews.review_text:
Tiger Yaki is such a vibe if you love good Asian food with a great atmosphere. We tried the spicy cottage cheese with noodles, vegetable pan-seared gyoza, and tofu katsu curry — and honestly, everything was on point. The spice was perfectly balanced, the noodles were super satisfying, and the gyoza had that ideal crispy-soft texture.

The sides added a nice fresh contrast, and the tofu katsu curry was rich and comforting. What made the experience even better was the warm, attentive service and the music, which really elevated the whole vibe. Wasim and Azhar were top notch with their service.

Overall, great food, great energy, and definitely a place worth going back to.

featured_reviews.name: Aniket
featured_reviews.review_text:
Tiger Yaki is an absolute hidden gem near Carter Road, Bandra, serving excellent Japanese and Korean food. It’s a no-fuss place with indoor AC and outdoor seating, where food is served in takeaway-style boxes and bowls. We visited as a group of six, including two kids, and loved everything we ordered—corn dog, veg and mushroom gyoza, tofu katsu curry, and mushroom and prawn takoyaki. The food was fresh, delicious, reasonably priced, service was excellent, toilets are available, though parking can be tricky.

Getting a good seat can be a challenge if you’re in a group of 4 and above. The indoor setting can sit just about 7 to 8 people so most of the times you’ll have to sit outside and face the heat and mosquitoes.
